Problem: Algorithms - 48
Prove the validity of the decomposition theorem for polyhedra by showing that every
polyhedron P admits the representation P = {x + c : x ∈X, c ∈C}, for some polytope
X and some polyhedral cone C.

0002 | Prove the validity of the decomposition theorem for polyhedra by showing that
0003 | every polyhedron P admits the representation P = {x+c : x ∈X, c ∈C}, for some polytope
0004 | X and some polyhedral cone C.
0005 | Solution: Decomposition Theorem for Polyhedra
0006 | Theorem 1 (Decomposition Theorem). Every polyhedron P ⊆Rn admits a representation
0007 | P = {x + c : x ∈X, c ∈C} = X + C
0008 | where X is a polytope and C is a polyhedral cone.
0009 | Definition 1.
0010 | • A polyhedron is a set P = {x ∈Rn : Ax ≤b} for some matrix
0011 | A ∈Rm×n and vector b ∈Rm.
0012 | • A polytope is a bounded polyhedron.
0013 | • A polyhedral cone is a set C = {x ∈Rn : Ax ≤0} for some matrix A.
0014 | • The recession cone of P is CP = {d ∈Rn : x + λd ∈P for all x ∈P, λ ≥0}.
0015 | Lemma 1. If P = {x : Ax ≤b} is a nonempty polyhedron, then its recession cone is
0016 | CP = {d : Ad ≤0}
0017 | which is a polyhedral cone.
0018 | Proof. Let d ∈CP. Then for any x ∈P and λ ≥0, we have x + λd ∈P, which means
0019 | A(x + λd) ≤b.
0020 | Since Ax ≤b, this gives λAd ≤0 for all λ ≥0. This implies Ad ≤0.
0021 | Conversely, suppose Ad ≤0. For any x ∈P with Ax ≤b and any λ ≥0:
0022 | A(x + λd) = Ax + λAd ≤b + λ · 0 = b
0023 | Thus x + λd ∈P for all x ∈P and λ ≥0, so d ∈CP.
0024 | Therefore CP = {d : Ad ≤0} is a polyhedral cone.
0025 | Lemma 2. The set X = P ∩{x : ∥x∥≤r} for sufficiently large r contains all extreme
0026 | points of P.
0027 | Proof. By the Minkowski-Weyl theorem, P has finitely many extreme points v1, . . . , vk.
0028 | Choose r > maxi=1,...,k ∥vi∥. Then all extreme points lie in the ball of radius r.
